common_name: Frosty Blue Whale's Tongue Agave (Powder-Blue Ovatifolia Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown transplants in spring in extremely well-drained, rocky or sandy soil in full sun to light shade; Frosty Blue is a selected clone chosen for an especially bright, powdery blue leaf color, so give it room to display its solitary rosette without crowding from neighboring plants.

directions: Frosty Blue is a named selection of whale's tongue agave singled out for a noticeably brighter, more intensely powdery blue leaf tone than typical seed-grown plants of the species, along with the same broad, deeply cupped, paddle-shaped leaves that give the species its common name. It forms a tight, solitary rosette that rarely offsets, so most nursery stock is propagated by tissue culture to preserve the selected color rather than grown from seed. Like the species it combines strong summer heat tolerance with real winter cold hardiness inherited from its high-elevation Mexican origin, making it well suited to Gulf Coast and Texas Hill Country landscapes where alkaline, fast-draining soil is available. Plants are monocarpic, flowering once on a tall branched stalk after a decade or more of growth before the rosette dies.

common_name: Ivory Tower Yucca (Compact Outward-Blooming Adam's Needle)

planting.note: Plant container-grown transplants or pups in spring in well-drained, sandy to average soil in full sun; Ivory Tower is a more compact selection of native Adam's needle chosen for a tighter rosette and flower spikes that hold their ivory-white bells facing outward rather than nodding downward.

directions: Ivory Tower is a compact cultivar of the native Adam's needle yucca, forming a tighter, stiffer rosette of thick, sword-shaped green leaves than the straight species while still producing the tall summer flower spike typical of the group. Its main distinction is floral: the large ivory-white, bell-shaped flowers are held more outward-facing along the spike rather than nodding downward, giving the bloom display a fuller, more visible presentation from a distance. Like the species it is extremely tolerant of heat, drought, salt spray, and poor sandy soils, needing essentially no supplemental water once established, which makes it a reliable structural accent for coastal and xeric plantings. Remove the spent flower stalk after bloom and separate basal offsets in spring if propagation is desired.
